rules: An avatar group shows the people (or teams) involved in an object as a row of overlapping avatars (the assignees of a task, the participants of a meeting, the members of a project), followed by a count of the others when there are too many.
size and shape apply to every Avatar of the group, including overflow; an avatar's own size and shape are ignored inside a group.

Avatars sit on one line in source order, each one overlapping the previous one by overlap and drawn above it, so that every avatar keeps its leading side whole and overflow, last, is never covered; each one is surrounded by a ring of ringWidth in ringColor following its shape, outside its box, which separates it from its neighbours. ringColor is the default surface; on another surface the integration gives the ring the color of that surface. The group never wraps.

The number of people is total when it is greater than the number of avatars given (the application knows more people than it shows), otherwise the number of avatars. When max is greater than 0 and that number exceeds max, the group shows the first max - 1 avatars followed by overflow, an Avatar in the fallback style whose initials are a plus sign followed by the number of the others (+3; +99 at most), so that the group never shows more than max boxes. With max 0 every avatar is shown and overflow appears only when total exceeds the number of avatars.

The group is exposed as a list named by label; each avatar keeps its own accessible name, and overflow is named by the number of the others followed by moreLabel (3 more). The group, its avatars and overflow are not interactive in this version: a list of everyone, or a profile on activation, is composed by the integration (a Popover or a Tooltip on a wrapping button).
In forced-colors mode each avatar keeps the edge of the Avatar and the ring uses the system background color, so that neighbours stay distinct.
